title: MemPalace/mempalace: local memory for coding agents, with no API key required
friendlyTitle: MemPalace stores an agent's past sessions on your own machine
summary: MemPalace is a local-first memory store for AI agents, MIT-licensed, at version 3.12.0. It keeps session text verbatim, searches it, and ships an MCP server plus plugins for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. The project says the core benchmark path needs no API key. It reports 96.6% Recall@5 on LongMemEval with zero API calls. Python 3.10 or newer is required. It is among the most-starred AI repositories trending today.
friendlySummary: MemPalace is a free memory store for AI agents. It keeps the text of past sessions and lets an agent search it. It includes plugins for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. The project says the main test path does not need an API key, and it reports a 96.6% score on a memory test called LongMemEval without calling an outside model. It needs Python 3.10 or newer. It is one of the most-starred AI projects trending today.
whyItMatters: Use it when an agent should look up an earlier session instead of guessing. The project names three official sources: this GitHub repository, the PyPI package, and mempalaceofficial.com, and it warns that other domains are not official. Embeddings can stay on your machine, or you can point them at an OpenAI-compatible server you run yourself.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Use it when you want an agent to look up what happened in an earlier session instead of guessing. The project says its only official homes are this GitHub repository, the PyPI package, and mempalaceofficial.com. Other websites using the name are not official. The search index can stay on your computer, or you can point it at a server you run yourself.
